videos.desc:

NOTE: All of the images for the friends are the images used from the publicly viewable profiles.

The rules are very simple.  All nodes repel each other.  All nodes are attracted toward me.  I am fixed. All nodes that are friends with each other generate a mass spring.  All friends then become attracted to each other.

videos.t: Low Latency USB AVR Sound Card
videos.desc:
We needed some very low latency sound output.  ALSA, Jack, etc... they couldn't do it.  Our solution was to make an AVR USB sound card.  It uses control messages.  So, we know exactly how much latency there is.

Additionally, we don't need to be realtime or use any other special extensions to get our period to 16, and a maximum buffer of 128.    Correction from video, it was actually 2.73 kHz, not 273 Hz.

Source (AVR and topside for Linux) https://cnlohr.net/pubsvn/electrical/avr_my32u/soundcard

videos.t: Capacitive coupling masks real design error
videos.desc:
See the video about this modded nintendo zapper: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=alBHtmm964E

In the development of my color-gun nintendo zapper mod, my trigger appeared to work, but seemed faulty, like the switch was bad.  When I clicked, it would only hold down momentarily.  Little did I know the bug was far stranger.

I was, in software looking at an adjacent pin.  It made me believe all was well because it was capacitively coupled to the right pin, when in fact the design was completely wrong.

The fix was as simple as changing the pin in firmware.

videos.t: Kelvin 50LE Multimeter vs 3,500 volts, 14' drop and more.
videos.desc:

So, some people didn't understand how deadly serious I was about Kelvin 50LEs being the best volt meters I've ever used.  They work when you put 1kV into them, they finally break somewhere between 1.5 and 2kV.  It takes more than 2A in the 200mA port to fry the current circuitry and even after a 14' drop, you can just tape the back back on and it works.

Just wait to see how I finally kill it.

videos.t: "Meteors" from landmark Atari lawsuit unveiled 30 years later.

Stephen Holniker, CEO of Amusement World passed away in October, 2012.

After 30 years, Eric Holniker, his son uncovered the actual Meteors arcade.

Check out The Save Point on facebook https://www.facebook.com/SavePointMD or come in and play the game!
